project_scope.note: Seven installed canonical concepts counted; M. piniflora source-concept ID and M. paniculata taxonomy/photo reviews remain flagged, not accepted as genus-key finished.

recognition.where_to_look_first: The project set spans large fountain-form bunchgrasses, small tight bunchgrasses, creeping nimblewill, and rhizomatous low muhly. Start with growth form and scale, then inspect the ligule, leaf folding/rolling, and panicle size and openness.
priority: upright bunchgrass versus creeping/rooting or rhizomatous habit
flat versus folded or involute blades
open feathery versus narrow contracted panicle
spikelet size and awn detail when the habit split is not enough

quick_split: M. lindheimeri — a LARGE coarse dense fountain clump with tall relatively contracted flower panicles and long membranous ligules.
M. reverchonii — SMALLER, more finely textured erect tuft with an airy, delicate panicle; compare true ligule and spikelet with lindheimeri.
M. schreberi — LOW weak creeping stems with short sideways leaves and narrow nearly spike-like panicle; may root from stolon nodes.
M. utilis — LOW rhizomatous grass with hair-fine inward-rolled leaves, SCALY underground rhizomes and small narrow often partly enclosed panicle.
M. paniculata (tumblegrass; formerly Schedonnardus paniculatus) — a few very LONG, slender, widely diverging one-sided racemes, often curving; look at branch shape instead of cloudlike plumes.
M. ×involuta — natural HYBRID of lindheimeri × reverchonii; intermediate stature/folded blades, but NEVER identify solely by parent-like habit.
M. piniflora — SOURCE NAME UNRESOLVED; not a taxonomically reliable field diagnosis or finished card.
comparison_lesson.nursery_warning: Do not use pink plume color by itself to call a plant M. lindheimeri. The widely sold M. capillaris concept is not a project-native Central Texas anchor.

visual_needs: PRIORITY PAIR: same-scale separately taxon-verified attached mature ligules for M. lindheimeri and M. reverchonii, measured with a millimeter ruler (published ranges partly overlap).
Actual aboveground stolon NODE ISSUING ROOTS for M. schreberi, plus a separate tiny ligule and contracted mature panicle.
Genuinely exposed underground SCALY RHIZOME, rolled leaf cross-section, and small mature inflorescence for M. utilis.
Paniculata: clear TWO ROWS of spikelets on ONE SIDE of slender divergent raceme; full plant and twisted leaves.
An exact taxon-correct, reuse-permitted, verified live M. ×involuta PHOTO; existing multigrass historic plate/parent pictures do not fill this gap.
Resolve the original source concept / scientific identity of M. piniflora before visual species-ID training.
Species-level lookalike closeup of M. lindheimeri, M. reverchonii and natural hybrid ×involuta on matched scale.
After newly added wild flowering photos, next highest diagnostic gap is a measured attached seep ligule and separated mature glumes/lemma/awn on the SAME plant.

M. piniflora remains excluded from fast-fill because its canonical record is scientifically PROVISIONAL and likely represents an erroneous source name. Do not pad wild-type lessons with named cultivars or uncertain-rights media.
look_here_first: MUHLY PHOTO-ID SEQUENCE — start at whole growth form: LARGE dense fountain + narrow contracted flowering heads (lindheimeri); SMALL tightly tufted hair-fine leaves + OPEN airy mature panicle (reverchonii); LOW jointed side-leaved stems (schreberi); extremely fine low patch requiring SCALY belowground rhizome (utilis); or conspicuous LONG divergent racemes (paniculata). SECOND use a fresh unfolded sheath/collar and measured membranous ligule, actual root-bearing surface node or underground rhizome where relevant, and mature spikelets. NEW three TRUE SEEP source-photographed OPEN panicles/spikelets now appear immediately after seep's fine foliage panels; dense narrow head in Lindheimer's own two photos belongs to Lindheimer. Compare open versus contracted panicle before measuring ligule. Hybrid ×involuta requires specimen-backed evidence; piniflora remains source-name HOLD.

comparison_matrix.title: Two upright muhly bunchgrasses — strongest structures
rows: Habit

Compact, finer, often ca. 0.4–0.8 m
Full rooted plant with ruler; sizes overlap
Leaf blades
Longer relatively coarse, 2–5 mm in many treatments
Very fine threadlike, around 1–2 mm
Fresh blade and ruler; maturity matters
Flowering head
Longer, commonly strongly contracted panicle packed with spikelets (verified head shape shown in our local photo)
Open, delicate branching mature panicle (expected botanically, not yet photographed in current source-identified seep archive)
Use the same verified flowering specimen and complete head side-on; existing Lindheimer head must NOT be treated as seep
Ligule
Usually conspicuous, long PAPERY membrane; GrassBase often 8–15 mm
Typically shorter PAPERY membrane; GrassBase 2–4(–9) mm
Open a mature attached blade–sheath junction and photograph ligule edge with mm scale; length is not completely non-overlapping
Tiny reproductive details
Usually one fertile floret; often short or absent lemma awn
Typically one fertile floret, awn often more evident
Dissect intact mature spikelets with scale
Pink coloration
May vary, not reliable
Can flush reddish, not reliable
Never ID from color alone
Evidence in CURRENT local gallery
Large dense fountain foliage + tan contracted flowering heads, no ligule macro
Now 2 fine seep foliage views PLUS 3 true wild OPEN flowering panicle/spikelet originals
Gross panicle architecture now photographed for both taxa. Same-plant collar/ligule and measured floret remains missing.
comparison_matrix.caution: Kew GrassBase describes Lindheimer ligules 8–15 mm and seep 2–4(–9) mm, with some local treatments reporting different lengths. DO NOT impose one hard 8-mm yes/no key; match several fresh leaves, full mature inflorescence and a magnified spikelet. The existing 4-photo pair is not a same-scale matched comparison, and new three wild seep flowering photographs now illustrate an open panicle, but the ligule and separated measured floret still need same-plant photography. Hybrid ×involuta can be intermediate and must not be forced from a normal size gradient. Cultivar photos are not wild local records.

genus_field_comparison_sets.title: Large fountain vs fine small tuft
genus_field_comparison_sets.compare: FIELD TEACHING ORDER: (1) whole upright crown/clump and mature complete head: Lindheimer big coarse fountain with comparatively contracted dense heads; seep smaller very fine tuft with OPEN delicate head; (2) unfold sheath/blade junction on the same living plant and measure true membranous ligule in mm, not a hard cutoff; (3) photograph individual one-flowered mature spikelet + awn; (4) check whether an intermediate plant could be the natural hybrid ×involuta rather than guessing. Our present four photos verify only Lindheimer bunch+heads and seep foliage, NOT seep blooms or either ligule.
